fields.Company Description: We straddle San Juan, Santo Domingo, and Punta Cana-adjacent assets—some flagged, some independent all-inclusive adjacent. Owners include US REIT slices and Caribbean families. We speak NEC and local labor law without mixing them up.
fields.Company Tagline: Island operations with stateside reporting hygiene.
fields.Mission Statement: Keep guests safe and owners informed when the grid blinks.
fields.cap_profile_operational: Security and beach operations meet brand and local law—guest journey protocols, night staffing, and vendor access rules documented for owners and insurers. Staff housing and transport are planned where markets are tight—because service failures from commute chaos become owner liability. QA blends life safety with guest experience; corrective actions are visible.
fields.cap_deep_execution_infra: Cybersecurity and data controls treated as operational risk—patch cadence, access reviews, and incident comms with owners when material. Shared services carry SKU-mapped chargebacks; quarterly reconciliation.
fields.mkt_signal_years: 7.3 yrs avg leadership tenure in core markets
fields.cap_card_governance: Committee structure for owners above agreed key-count thresholds; minority protections and consent rights documented in the management agreement.
fields.cap_card_execution_rel: Single owner-facing timeline across operations, finance, and brand—no duplicate narratives in different departments.
fields.cap_profile_transition: Week one prioritizes life safety, cash, payroll, and insurance interfaces—brand and RMS follow with dated milestones lenders can track. Business interruption assumptions and deductibles are modeled with owners before close, not after a claim. Handbacks mirror the same discipline.
fields.cap_card_service_diff: F&B and spa programming tuned to ADR and capture rate; where F&B is a profit center, we staff for consistency; where it is amenity-driven, we protect margin.
fields.specificMarkets: Mexico City, Cancún, Monterrey, Guadalajara, San José (Costa Rica), Panama City, Bogotá, Medellín, Lima, Santiago, Montevideo, Santo Domingo, San Juan.
fields.cap_card_asset_positioning: Urban gateway and resort leisure mix balanced by micro-market; ADR strategy tied to comp sets and airlift or corporate demand drivers, not generic brand tiers.
fields.cap_profile_commercial: Group, casino-adjacent, and corporate segments carry distinct playbooks—pace horizons match sales capacity; discounting requires rationale tied to GOP. Owners see channel economics with loyalty and OTA load transparent—no vanity top line that collapses in diligence.
fields.mkt_narrative_depth: San Juan corporate and leisure, Santo Domingo urban, east coast resort leisure—different staffing and promo calendars.
fields.cap_deep_revenue_systems: Enterprise RMS with channel cost and loyalty transparency; group pace and transient strategy tie to one forecast. Owner packs show net contribution after distribution—critical where brands and OTAs interlock.
fields.ownerEngagementNarrative: We split the narrative: US-based owners and investors get GAAP-friendly reconciliation and board-ready decks; local owners get operational truth in plain language—same numbers, different depth. Lenders see covenant monitoring and outage scenarios because Puerto Rico and the Dominican Republic are not theoretical for us. Brand partners get QA tied to life safety and backup power—because guest incidents are brand incidents. We do not promise perfection; we promise named escalation paths, documented runbooks, and post-event reviews owners can share with their boards.
fields.idealProjectsAdditionalNotes: Prefer assets with clear GOP history or defensible proforma.
fields.ov_card_commercial: Commercial engine connects group, casino-adjacent, and transient strategies to GOP with promo discipline—owners see margin trade on every major discount proposal.
fields.pipRepositioningDetails: PIP schedules aligned to brand; owner-funded with caps.
fields.ov_card_discipline: Procurement, vendor access, and exception logs reviewed with institutional owners monthly—storm scopes pre-negotiated where possible. Related-party services benchmarked.
fields.ownerPortalFeatures: Real-time GOP flash, document vault, capex tracker, brand QA.
fields.renewalConditions: No uncured default; PIP complete; fees current; brand in good standing.
fields.incentiveExcessNotes: Preferred return waterfall on two JV assets.
fields.bf_not_ideal_for: Mandates where the owner requires daily operational involvement without a governance framework—we work best with clear thresholds and scheduled touchpoints.
fields.incentiveFeeNotes: Hurdle over GOP budget; clawback provisions standard.
fields.decisionMaking: Threshold matrix in MSA; >$50k capex requires owner consent unless emergency.
fields.mgmtFeeNotes: Tiered by GOP performance band with hurdle definitions in exhibit schedules.
fields.ov_card_flexibility: Consent matrices for capex and fuel contracts; flexibility lives in schedules—no handshake deals that fracture on portfolio sale.
fields.ov_card_communication: Weekly flash in storm season; monthly GAAP-friendly financials; same-day sponsor for material outage or cash events. Boards receive post-event summaries they can file.
fields.ov_cluster_interaction: Steering committees for assets in transition; charter defines quorum, minutes, and decision rights.
fields.ov_cluster_deliverables: Same-day flash when GOP variance exceeds agreed threshold; escalation path names a single executive sponsor.
fields.additionalNotes: Antillano Norte: USVI/PR power grid and DR all-inclusive labor cadence called out in calls.
fields.disputeResolution: Escalation: GM → RVPO → executive sponsor → optional mediation.
fields.knownRedFlags: Before signing we flag single-asset concentration, FX mismatch between revenue and debt service, and sticky employment or vendor clauses—reviewed with Antillano Norte Hospitality Group's counsel and documented for owners.
fields.esgExpectations: LEED / EarthCheck alignment where brand permits; water reporting in arid markets.
fields.ov_card_risk: Named wind deductibles, BI assumptions, and fuel reserves in packs pre-season; mutual aid across islands for staffing and supplies. Escalation routes short and documented.
fields.ownerNonNegotiableOther: Legacy vendor or labor clauses are surfaced in diligence with remediation dates and owners' counsel sign-off—Antillano Norte Hospitality Group tracks through close.
fields.ownerNonNegotiables: No undisclosed related-party vendors; all rebates shared per contract.
fields.baseFeeEscalationHow: CPI capped at 3% annually in USD contracts.
fields.capexSupport: Structured reserves; brand PIP coordination; owner approval gates.
fields.bf_signal_capital: Comfortable with PIP-heavy and key money structures.
fields.ownerEarlyTerminationNotes: For-cause and convenience paths with fee true-up schedules aligned to lender requirements where applicable.
fields.bf_operating_situations: Stabilized, conversion, new build, and distressed transition with documented mobilization plans.
fields.performanceMetricsOther: Labor hours per occupied room and channel cost as percent of room revenue—reviewed monthly with Antillano Norte Hospitality Group and tied to incentive hurdles where applicable.
fields.centralServiceAllocationsNotes: Allocations by key count; reconciled quarterly.
fields.majorLenders: Regional banks and multilaterals—references available under NDA.
fields.preOpeningFeesNotes: Capped % of revenues months -3 to +6 from opening.
fields.industryRecognition: STR benchmark leadership in select markets; brand excellence citations and owner-nominated service awards where properties compete regionally.
feeExpectationVsMarket: Open to incentive structures / performance fees
fields.infra_systems_technology: Cloud PMS, integrated POS, data lake for owner BI.
fields.mkt_signal_fte: 4.2 FTE per 100 keys (portfolio average, trailing twelve)
fields.serviceDifferentiators: National and regional procurement leverage with CALA labor pools shared across assets; owners see savings and chargebacks transparently.
fields.lead_signal_succession: Documented for CEO and COO roles.
fields.risk_programs_narrative: Enterprise risk register reviewed quarterly; internal audit rotation; brand compliance scoring tied to incentive hurdles where contracts require.
fields.apiIntegrations: REST to owner data room; SFTP for lenders.
fields.certifications: ISO 9001 internal program; LEED AP on staff.
fields.infra_asset_management_reporting: Monthly AM pack: KPI tree, capex, risk register.
fields.lead_narrative_resilience: Succession plans for RVPs; cross-training Mexico ↔ Caribbean.
fields.systems_inventory_lines: PMS, CRS, RMS, POS, HRIS, GL, and owner data-room integrations—inventory reviewed annually with cybersecurity assessment.
fields.diligenceDocumentLinks: Indexed data room path issued after NDA—request schedule for cala-ten-antillano-norte via investor relations.

caseStudiesDetail.services: We sequenced generator, roof, and public-area work around forecasted occupancy and event calendars; staged contractor access, guest communication, and contingency operating procedures; and aligned spend releases with lender and owner milestones so each tranche of capex had a clear operating rationale.
caseStudiesDetail.outcome: We sequenced generator, roof, and public-area capex around occupancy so cash and guest safety stayed aligned—no vanity reopen dates. RevPAR versus the owner's chosen competitive set improved 8 points over twelve rolling months; GOP margin expanded 160 bps in the same window as labor productivity improved 7% measured as rooms revenue per paid hour.
caseStudiesDetail.owner_relevance: Reference for select-service owners balancing renovation timing, lender reporting, and operating continuity in airport/leisure submarkets.

caseStudiesDetail.services: We redesigned beach and pool F&B with simplified menus, standardized prep and service sequences, and labor models tied to forecasted covers by daypart. We retrained beach and kitchen leads, reset vendor and inventory controls, and introduced weekly outlet P&L reviews with the owner.
caseStudiesDetail.outcome: Redesigned beach and pool F&B with simplified menus and labor models tied to peak-day demand; guest satisfaction scores rose 11 points and repeat-stay revenue grew 19% in the first season after rollout.
caseStudiesDetail.owner_relevance: Illustrates independent resort turnaround where owner value is driven by experience and F&B mix—not brand affiliation.

caseStudiesDetail.services: We reset the commercial strategy end to end: rebuilt the group and corporate contracting pipeline, repriced banquet and catering packages, tightened transient channel mix, and instituted a weekly owner reporting cadence that tied revenue actions to GOP and F&B profit drivers—not just occupancy headlines.
caseStudiesDetail.outcome: GOP margin expanded 210 basis points year over year; group room revenue grew 23% while total F&B profit dollars rose 17% in the first full year post-program.
caseStudiesDetail.owner_relevance: Relevant for institutional owners of branded urban full-service hotels in CALA gateway cities evaluating operator-led commercial resets without a full repositioning capex cycle.

ownerDiligenceQa.question: How do you summarize your operating experience across property types, brands, and situations (e.g. new builds, conversions, transitions, stabilized assets)? What do you typically make available to validate that experience?
ownerDiligenceQa.answer: We operate resorts and full-service/select-service in Puerto Rico and the Dominican Republic—transitions, stabilizations, new wings. Post-NDA: references, STR, and management fee exhibits.

ownerDiligenceQa.question: How do you generally handle owner references, introductions, and credibility checks for prospective partners? What is your typical process and timing?
ownerDiligenceQa.answer: References: coordinated with owners; asset-type matched; NDAs respected.

ownerDiligenceQa.question: What financial and operational information do owners typically receive, on what cadence, and through what channels?
ownerDiligenceQa.answer: Reporting: weekly flash in storm season; monthly financials; board packs for institutional owners.

ownerDiligenceQa.question: At a high level, how do you describe typical termination rights, notice and cure, and standards for operational handback—without referencing a single deal?
ownerDiligenceQa.answer: Exit: documented handback—data, staff notices, brand offboarding checklist.

ownerDiligenceQa.question: How is revenue management organized (in-house, hybrid, or outsourced), which primary systems do you use, and how do owners stay informed or involved?
ownerDiligenceQa.answer: Revenue: central RM support; property execution; owner call optional.

ownerDiligenceQa.question: How do you recruit, transition, and retain general managers and other critical roles? How do you maintain bench depth and continuity across the portfolio?
ownerDiligenceQa.answer: Bench: regional GM pool; cross-training between islands where visas allow.

ownerDiligenceQa.question: What is your standard approach to assuming management—key milestones, workstreams, and staffing—in the first weeks and months after engagement?
ownerDiligenceQa.answer: Transitions: life safety and cash day one; brand and RMS within 30–60 days; staffing plans shared.

ownerDiligenceQa.question: How do you typically approach owner-funded capital, brand-required improvements, reserves, and deferred maintenance in the ordinary course of management?
ownerDiligenceQa.answer: Capital: PIPs and FF&E—approval matrix with owners.

ownerDiligenceQa.question: Which KPIs and benchmarks do you routinely monitor, share with owners, and use for performance discussions or incentive alignment?
ownerDiligenceQa.answer: KPIs: RevPAR, GOP, labor, guest scores, channel mix—incentives per contract.

ownerDiligenceQa.question: How are management fees, central or allocated charges, and reconciliations generally structured, documented, and disputed if needed?
ownerDiligenceQa.answer: Fees: US-style schedules with clear central charges; dispute path in exhibit.
